similarities.point: Both describe Olney as a market town in Buckinghamshire.
similarities.quote_britannica: OULENEY, a market-town of Buckinghamshire, situated nine miles South-east of Northampton.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Olney (/ ˈ oʊ n i /, rarely / ˈ ɒ l n i / OW -nee, rarely OLL -nee, the "L" is not pronounced by local people) is a market town and civil parish in the unitary authority area of the City of Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire, England.

similarities.point: Both mention the town's distance from Northampton.
similarities.quote_britannica: OULENEY, a market-town of Buckinghamshire, situated nine miles South-east of Northampton.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Lying on the left bank of the River Great Ouse, the Town is located around 8 miles (13 km) from Milton Keynes, and 10 miles (16 km) from Bedford, Northampton and Wellingborough.

wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: Late Jurassic dinosaur bones were unearthed at a quarry near Clifton Reynes. Evidence of Neolithic, Bronze and Iron Age activity has been found in and around Olney, much of it close to the River Ouse.

wiki_only_topics.topic: The Olney Hymns and notable residents
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: Olney is best known for poet William Cowper, anti-slavery preacher John Newton, and their 1770's collaboration the Olney Hymns, including Amazing Grace (see History, below).
Olney was a centre of the Buckinghamshire lace-making industry, noted in 1769 for 'considerable Manufacture of Bone-lace'.
Since 1445, a pancake race has been run in the Town on many Pancake Days, the day before the beginning of Lent.
Olney has been part of the Borough (now City) of Milton Keynes since 1974, which has been a unitary authority since 1997.
